language.script_notes: Spanish appears bilingually on signage in Arizona/New Mexico/Texas border areas; Native American place names common (Navajo, Hopi, Pueblo).
false_friends: Central Asia/Middle East deserts in generic desert imagery

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on mountain highways; wooden posts in National Parks, painted medium brown by park-service convention.
road_furniture.line_paint: Long straight desert highways with wide gravel shoulders.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal or absent in rural desert areas; xeriscaped (rock/gravel, not grass) yards common in residential areas even where curbs exist.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Taller, more widely spaced poles across open desert; wide, empty road shoulders.

architecture.roof_style: Flat or very low-pitch roofs on Southwest adobe/pueblo-style buildings; simple gable roofs on standard suburban stock in Denver/Phoenix.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile in Spanish/Pueblo-revival architecture (especially New Mexico, southern Arizona).
architecture.wall_construction: Adobe or stucco construction with rounded corners and earth-tone colour is the signature Southwest look (especially Santa Fe/Taos style); standard wood-frame suburban stock elsewhere in the region.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm earth tones — tan, terracotta, dusty pink stucco — is the strongest single Southwest architectural tell.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Flat-roofed adobe/pueblo-style buildings with rounded stucco corners and exposed roof beams (vigas); Spanish mission-style churches; ski-town architecture in Rocky Mountain resort areas; casino/resort architecture in Nevada.

nature.vegetation: Sagebrush and scrub desert vegetation; saguaro cacti are a near-unique tell for the Sonoran Desert (Arizona specifically); piñon-juniper woodland at higher elevation; alpine conifer forest in the Rockies.
nature.terrain: Iconic red sandstone formations and canyons on the Colorado Plateau (Arizona/Utah/Colorado); vast arid basins and mesas; the Rocky Mountains rising sharply with snow-capped peaks; the Grand Canyon/Monument Valley style red-rock landscape is instantly recognizable.
nature.climate_signature: Bright, dry, intense sunlight with a red/orange/tan colour palette in the desert; harsh alpine winters at elevation in the Rockies; very sparse vegetation and long horizon sightlines.

vehicles.plate_color: Varies by state — Arizona plate with a purple accent bottom-right, Colorado green mountain-themed plate, Utah red-rock-arch themed plate, New Mexico yellow-and-red 'zia symbol' plate, Nevada silver/blue.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Jeeps and off-road-capable SUVs more common given terrain; RVs common near National Parks.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations; dense modern coverage around Phoenix/Denver/Las Vegas, thinner and sometimes older on remote desert/mountain roads.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good highway coverage but genuine gaps across remote desert backroads and National Park interiors.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Sonoran/Chihuahuan desert vegetation and terrain right across the border, similar adobe/stucco architecture and earth-tone palette
confusion_set.tiebreaker: US plates, yellow center lines and English (with bilingual Spanish) signage vs. Mexican plates and Spanish-only signage; road paving/maintenance quality is generally more consistent on the US side.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, some shared desert terrain in inland California/Nevada
confusion_set.tiebreaker: This region's red-rock Colorado Plateau and saguaro-studded Sonoran Desert look is distinct from the Pacific region's conifer forest, redwood coastline and coastal vegetation.
